subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Which canonical Discord message permissions and defaults should replace the coarse `actions.messages` gate, and how should existing boolean values migrate?
rationale: The source-level gap is proven, but this changes a stable channel's operator authorization boundary and persisted configuration contract; safe defaults and upgrade semantics require maintainer intent.

options.title: Granular permissions with migration
options.body: Add explicit send, read, edit, and delete permissions and doctor-migrate each old boolean to equivalent all-enabled or all-disabled values.

options.title: Keep send outside optional actions
options.body: Leave normal outbound send available and independently gate read, edit, delete, and related optional message operations.

options.title: Retain the coarse gate
options.body: Preserve one message permission and only make send discovery and runtime behavior consistent.

recommendation.title: Granular permissions with migration
recommendation.body: Add explicit send, read, edit, and delete permissions and doctor-migrate each old boolean to equivalent all-enabled or all-disabled values.

likelyOwner.reason: They previously reviewed this exact decision and have concrete history in the Discord config contract that must change.
